title: An Information-Geometric Framework for Probabilistic Grammars and Rank-Frequency Scaling Dynamics
content: We develop an information-geometric framework modeling the continuous evolution of probabilistic grammars as variational trajectories on a statistical manifold endowed with the Fisher–Rao metric, and investigate when these flows exhibit power-law rank–frequency scaling. Idealized grammar evolution is postulated to follow Fisher geodesics, representing a variational modeling hypothesis rather than a consequence of the metric itself. Asymptotic scaling is characterized via rank-dilation covariance: if \( p(\lfloor\lambda r\rfloor)/p(r) \to \lambda^{-\alpha} \) for all \( \lambda > 0 \), Karamata’s regular variation theory implies \( p(r) = r^{-\alpha}L(r) \) with \( L \) slowly varying, independent of manifold geometry. To link parameter-space geometry and rank-space scaling, we formulate a falsifiable Geometric Scaling Conjecture. For a Gibbs family \( p_n(\beta) \propto e^{-\beta E_n} \) with an asymptotically logarithmic spectrum \( E_n \sim \log n \), rank-dilation covariance holds for \( \beta > 1 \) with \( \alpha = \beta \), and Fisher geodesics dictate the evolution speed of \( \alpha(s) = \beta(s) \). For the zeta distribution, \( g_{\beta\beta} \sim (\beta-1)^{-2} \) as \( \beta \to 1^+ \), placing the classical Zipf boundary \( \alpha=1 \) at infinite Fisher distance. Finally, regular and multi-agent grammar examples demonstrate how grammatical coupling induces non-flat Fisher curvature and prices state transitions.
